blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is legal in this country, but the state barely exists outside the capital; armed groups control most territory; mob violence and police extortion against perceived LGBT people are documented; no LGR, no community infrastructure.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: only an international legal-aid trust's homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no country-specific page); the trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people. This country does not criminalise same-sex conduct but has no protections.
A global LGBT-rights organisation's 2023 world report on laws criminalising LGBT people; the fetched copy contained no extractable text at research time (image-based PDF).

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the SOGI section - same-sex conduct not criminalised but societal discrimination and the absence of protections in a conflict-affected state.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on this country: documents extrajudicial killings, torture and rape by security forces and rebel militias, harsh prison conditions - general human-rights context with limited LGBT-specific content.

LGBT-rights news project overview (May 2019) of LGBT rights in five countries of this region, by regional activists - SOGI issues remain taboo and are called 'contrary to prevailing cultural values'; one neighbouring state kept its criminalising provision; this country has a legal vacuum; walking the streets as a same-sex couple is visibly difficult across the region.

UN human-rights office summary of stakeholders' submissions for this country's universal periodic review (45th session, Jan 2024): covers international obligations, national human-rights framework, institutional infrastructure - includes SOGI-related stakeholder recommendations.
